section_summary: This section finishes a National Engineers Committee report recommending limits on Japanese industries considered capable of supporting rearmament, while preserving production needed for civilian life. It then gives the report’s appendix list, committee membership, a detailed survey of Japan’s mineral and metal industries, and the beginning of statistical tables on world nitrogen production and consumption.

subfiles.title: National Engineers Committee report on Japan’s industrial war potential
subfiles.about: Recommendations for limiting Japanese industrial capacity to civilian needs and preventing rearmament.
subfiles.summary: The report sets proposed production ceilings and controls for steel, aluminum, magnesium, copper, lead, zinc, tin, machine tools, chemicals, coal, petroleum, synthetic oil and electric power. It links essential fertilizer, fuel and material supplies to civilian recovery while recommending the removal or licensing of facilities with military uses. Its closing sections call for controls on research, nuclear energy, new construction, imports and fabrication, backed by technical inspectors and a continuing policing force.

subfiles.title: Appendices
subfiles.about: Lists the report’s appendices on committees and Japanese mineral, chemical, fuel and power industries.

subfiles.title: Appendix I-A: Engineers Joint Council, 1945–1946
subfiles.about: Names engineering society officers and the Engineers Joint Council executive committee.
subfiles.summary: Roster of society officers and executive committee members.

subfiles.title: Appendix I-B: National Engineers Committee and Task Committees
subfiles.about: Names the administrative, control and specialist task committee members.
subfiles.summary: Roster of committee members and chairs.

subfiles.title: Appendix II: Japan’s Mineral and Metal Industries
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese mineral resources, metal production and imports under proposed peacetime industrial limits.
subfiles.summary: The appendix opens with an iron and steel discussion, repeated on pages 98–99, then provides plant capacities and historical consumption tables. It surveys copper, lead, zinc, tin, nickel, ferroalloy minerals, precious metals and industrial minerals, using production and import figures to assess civilian needs. It discusses where import controls might limit military capacity and where domestic production or imports would support fertilizers and consumer goods.

subfiles.title: Appendix III-A, Table I: World Nitrogen Productive Capacity
subfiles.about: Estimates 1944 national nitrogen capacity and compares projected postwar world capacity with 1938 consumption.
subfiles.summary: Capacity table with source notes and an estimate of more than one million short tons of postwar excess capacity.

subfiles.title: Appendix III-A, Table II: World Nitrogen Statistics—Capacity and Production
subfiles.about: Tabulates world nitrogen capacity and production by process from 1924 through the early 1940s.
subfiles.summary: Historical capacity and production figures with source and conversion notes.

subfiles.title: Appendix III-A, Table II: World Nitrogen Statistics—Consumption
subfiles.about: Tabulates world nitrogen consumption in agriculture and industry from 1924 to 1938.
subfiles.summary: Consumption figures and period averages with source notes.
